passage:
Saturday, 10 pm.

Dad moved out today. His bags were by the door at nine and the car left before lunch. Mum kept saying "we're all fine" in a bright voice. I said I was fine too. I wasn't. I went to the bathroom, turned on the tap and cried until my head ached.

Still set my alarm. Still did homework. It helps to have things that stay the same.

Told Vandana at lunch. She didn't say anything smart, just sat next to me on the steps and let me cry a bit more. She's going to come over tomorrow.

I keep thinking of our old Sundays. I miss a family that turns out not to have been there. It's my loss too.

Payal

qa.q: What time were Dad's bags by the door?
qa.a: His bags were by the door at nine.

qa.q: What was Payal feeling when saying "fine" and then going to the bathroom to cry?
qa.a: Payal was grieving and sad, and said "fine" to match Mum's bright voice.

qa.q: What did Payal do that helps with coping?
qa.a: Payal cried instead of holding it in, kept the alarm and homework routine, and told Vandana about it.

qa.q: What might Vandana have been thinking as she sat on the steps without saying anything?
qa.a: Perhaps that there were no right words and that staying close mattered more than advice, so she simply sat with Payal and let the crying happen. 🤍

grounding: Shows a teen mourning the family they thought they had, letting the tears come, keeping routines and confiding in a friend.
